claims.text: The anomalous stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr arises primarily from temperature-dependent lattice distortion.
Thermal-expansion mismatch at heterogeneous microstructural features amplifies lattice distortion.
Casting followed by rolling and annealing produces a homogenized, single-phase HfNbTaTiZr solid solution with minimized precipitates.
Aging HfNbTaTiZr at 600–800 °C induces nanoscale precipitates or compositionally segregated regions.
The precipitates or segregated regions have thermal-expansion coefficients different from that of the surrounding matrix.
Differential thermal expansion between the matrix and heterogeneous regions generates internal stresses during heating.
Mismatch-generated internal stresses alter dislocation mobility.
Mismatch-enhanced lattice distortion modifies the elastic moduli.
The proposed mismatch mechanism accounts for the reported high-temperature creep behavior at 1250 °C.
The proposed mismatch mechanism accounts for microhardness changes during cold rolling.
The proposed mismatch mechanism accounts for elastic-modulus variations over a wide temperature range.
Aging-induced heterogeneous features provide additional barriers to dislocation motion.
The additional heterogeneous features raise yield strength relative to the homogenized baseline.
The additional heterogeneous features modify work-hardening behavior relative to the homogenized baseline.
The aged alloy will exhibit increased high-temperature yield strength relative to the homogenized alloy.
The aged alloy will exhibit modified creep behavior at 1250 °C relative to the homogenized alloy.
The aged alloy will exhibit greater lattice strain than the homogenized alloy.
The aged alloy will exhibit modified elastic moduli over the intermediate-temperature range.
Differences between aged and homogenized samples will be most pronounced at 600–800 °C because thermal-expansion mismatch is maximized there.
Below 600 °C, thermal-expansion effects are minimal.
